assetType: original historical 2D RTS unit sprite atlases

prompts.a:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: production sprite atlas for an original 2D historical RTS browser game, not concept portraits.
Input references: Image1 and Image2 are our original unit concepts; Image3 is the town-center raster atlas already used in the game. Match their richly painted semi-realistic material fidelity and muted historical color palette.
Render a TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA PNG portrait atlas with EXACTLY 4 columns and 8 rows, 32 separate isolated sprites. Prefer 1600x3200 pixels with 400x400 square cells. No visible grid, no labels, no writing, no background color or checkerboard.
Each row is ONE unit type, four consistent views of the same person/mount/equipment. Column1: facing diagonally toward lower-right screen (SE, front right three-quarter). Column2: facing diagonally toward lower-left screen (SW, front left three-quarter). Column3: facing diagonally away toward upper-right screen (NE, back right three-quarter: show the person's back). Column4: facing diagonally away toward upper-left screen (NW, back left three-quarter: show the person's back).
Use a downward-looking orthographic isometric game camera with 30-degree elevation and 2:1 ground projection. ALL four views must use that SAME camera; rotate the entire character or mount, not merely the head. Back views genuinely reveal clothing backs, rear helmet, quivers, horse rump and tail as appropriate.
The character's foot/hoof contact pivot is centered horizontally at 50% of each cell and at 84% of cell height. Put each complete figure/equipment inside the central 70% of its cell width and 76% of its cell height, with large completely empty transparent gutters. Every spear, bow, horse tail, helmet and foot fully inside its own cell. Absolutely no overlap, no clipped weapons and no pixels touching adjacent cells. One actor/machine only per cell, no ground island or vignette.
Art quality: mature believable adult anatomy about7.5heads tall, heads anatomically small relative to full body, natural leg length and hand proportions. Realistic detailed woven linen, wool folds, leather straps, scratched metal, woodgrain, skin tones, individual horse hair. Controlled highlights/ambient occlusion, soft upper-left daylight, detailed readable silhouettes that remain good after reduction to 45–65 game pixels. Stylized historical illustration with realistic proportions, NOT cartoon, NOT flat vector, NOT paper dolls, NOT chibi, NOT oversized heads, NOT chunky toys.
Team details: natural brown/linen base clothing for shared units, only a restrained small turquoise belt/sash. Unique civilization units have their characteristic clothing and equipment from the references. No logos, no real modern insignia, no watermark. Only extremely faint tight contact shadows, outside otherwise completely clear transparent alpha. No floating particles/debris or fringe.
ATLAS A — foot units. Rows EXACTLY in this order top to bottom:
1. Roman villager: adult Mediterranean laborer in modest off-white knee-length linen tunic, leather belt/sandals, short dark hair, carrying a short wooden-handled hoe. Natural muscular but ordinary body.
2. Mongol villager: adult Central Asian laborer in beige wool deel, fur-edged practical cap, brown trousers and boots, carrying a small pickaxe at rest.
3. Persian villager: adult West Asian laborer in muted rust-brown long tunic, plain linen soft cap, trousers and ankle boots, carrying a woven basket against chest.
4. Tang Chinese villager: adult East Asian laborer in desaturated blue-gray work tunic, dark trousers, simple tied hair, boots, carrying a compact bundle of timber on one shoulder.
5. Ottoman villager: adult West Asian laborer in cream work tunic and trousers, modest white wrap with dark red cap, leather belt and boots, holding a short mallet at rest.
6. Shared spear infantry: adult soldier wearing neutral linen tunic, subdued leather vest and modest iron helmet, round brown wooden shield, upright steel-tipped spear kept INSIDE cell. Small turquoise waist sash, no fancy faction insignia.
7. Shared sword-and-shield infantry: adult soldier in modest iron/leather armor over beige linen, short steel sword held low, practical round wooden shield, brown boots, small turquoise waist sash.
8. Shared archer: adult soldier in brown/linen padded garment, leather belt and boots, modest iron cap, wooden recurve bow at rest and quiver on back, small turquoise sash.
Every figure must be fully rendered head to feet. No horses in this atlas. Preserve consistency of the same figure across four views.

ATLAS B — mounted and faction units. Rows EXACTLY in this order top to bottom:
1. Scout: lightly equipped adult rider in brown travel tunic, small leather cap and turquoise sash, riding a realistic bay horse with simple saddle and bridle. Entire horse and rider, no raised weapon.
2. Light cavalry: adult rider in modest leather/mail vest and iron cap, short saber at rest, small round shield, on a realistic chestnut horse with simple saddle, restrained turquoise cloth.
3. Trader: adult traveling merchant in brown/linen robes walking beside a SINGLE compact realistic pack mule carrying two balanced woven panniers and folded cloth, no cart. Merchant+mule form one compact cohesive sprite, tied lead rope, all feet aligned to cell. Detailed trade packs.
4. Roman legionary: mature Roman soldier in realistic segmented iron armor and off-white short tunic, sandals, simple crest helmet, short gladius held low, large RED RECTANGULAR curved shield with restrained original gold motif. Adult proportions like references.
5. Roman engineer: adult Roman workman in off-white tunic, practical bronze helmet and leather tool apron, compact hammer, measuring staff and hanging tools. Natural body proportions, no oversized equipment.
6. Mongol horse archer: adult Central Asian rider in blue-brown wool and lamellar armor, fur-edged conical helmet, recurve bow held across chest, quiver at back, riding a realistic sturdy brown steppe horse. Blue accents match reference.
7. Mongol lancer: adult Central Asian rider in blue lamellar armor and fur-trimmed helmet, compact upright steel-tipped lance, riding a realistic tan/brown steppe horse with leather harness. Keep ENTIRE lance inside cell.
8. Persian guard: adult West Asian elite infantry in detailed muted-blue patterned coat and layered light scale armor, characteristic tall simple cap, elegant gold/brown oval shield and compact upright spear kept inside cell.
Horses/mule must have natural skeletal proportions, slim articulated legs and realistic long neck/head; never look like wooden toys or caricatures. Each view rotates complete actor and mount.

ATLAS C — elite, elephant and siege units. Rows EXACTLY in this order top to bottom:
1. Persian guard archer: mature West Asian archer in rich muted-blue woven patterned coat with gold edging, practical tall cap, bow held ready, quiver at back, dark ankle boots. Exactly same design across all four directions.
2. Persian war elephant: realistic large adult Asian elephant, gray wrinkled skin, proportionate legs, ears and trunk, ivory tusks, muted-blue-and-gold woven caparison and wooden howdah with one mahout and one guard. Detailed believable animal anatomy. Entire elephant+tusk+trunk+riders inside its cell.
3. Tang vanguard spearman: mature East Asian soldier in dark iron lamellar armor over subdued red tunic, dark trousers and brown boots, modest crested helmet, long red-tasseled spear held diagonally but fully contained in cell. Adult anatomy, no giant helmet.
4. Tang armored heavy cavalry: mature East Asian rider in red and iron lamellar armor with modest helmet, realistic dark brown horse wearing articulated iron/leather barding, short spear at rest, natural proportionate horse anatomy. Like reference.
5. Ottoman musketeer: mature West Asian soldier in muted-red coat, cream trousers, leather belt and boots, restrained tall white/red felt cap, carrying a historic matchlock musket aimed slightly downward. Fine wood/metal details, no smoke or firing effects.
6. Ottoman cannon with crew: compact patinated BRONZE field cannon on a believable timber wheeled carriage, two mature human crew in green/cream work garments with modest wraps, arranged tightly together as one sprite. All crew and muzzle/wheels fully inside cell.
7. Battering ram: compact historical timber wheeled siege ram with a sloped protective leather/timber roof and iron-capped central timber ram, believable carpentry, NO giant fortress. No crew needed.
8. Catapult: compact historical timber wheeled stone-throwing catapult, sturdy triangular beams, ropes, sling and throwing arm, believable wood/metal detail. No crew needed.
Use consistent miniature 2:1 isometric scale and four complete rotated views for each elephant/machine. No foreground scene, platform, arrows in flight, people separated from their designated siege sprite, explosions, text or UI.

grid.sourceAlignment: Regular visual4x8 layout with some position/weapon drift. Runtime uses measured subject frames rather than fixed grid cuts.
grid.measurement: Read-only connected-component bounds with alpha>=200 and2px safe padding. Merchant and mule are combined into one source frame. No offline image editing or alpha changes were made.

portrait.source: Direct high-resolution source-frame sampling, rather than a magnified world sprite.

runtime.motion: Four frame indices provide only subpixel sway and bob. The generated views are static paintings, not an authored gait animation.
runtime.scale: Fixed per type across all4views. Adult bodies46–47px; mounted bodies59–61px; elephant84px; siege63–65px. Long weapons may extend above these body heights.
runtime.pivot: Human horizontal pivot estimated from opaque pixels in the lower quarter; mounted/elephant/siege pivot is horizontal center. Vertical pivot is placed slightly above nearest foot/hoof/wheel contact to approximate the ground center. Exact canvas anchors remain stable.
runtime.teamMarker: Prototype ground pennant removed from current v7 runtime at user request; no per-unit flag.
runtime.age: Type/class selects equipment. These atlases do not add extra per-age unit variants.

rights.origin: Generated using original project AI unit concepts and the original town-center atlas as style references; no downloaded third-party art.
rights.commercialUse: Subject to applicable OpenAI terms and law, consistent with ../../docs/en/RIGHTS-AND-LICENSES.md.
rights.note: AI output is not guaranteed exclusive, unique, or copyrightable; this manifest supplies provenance rather than a legal warranty.

provenancePathPolicy: Repository-relative paths identify retained source files. generation-record: identifies an unbundled tool output. Original tool paths are kept only in ignored local records. Unused concept boards and user-reference photographs have been removed.
removedDesignInputs: Reference images and draft inputs were used during creation. Unused original inputs have been removed and are not distributed.
